title: A task that proves each step
statement: In independent practice, still walk the taught procedure, giving each step a small task that shows the learner did it.
example: Four small tasks walk one reading procedure: click what you are looking for, click the first line to reread, tap the evidence, then fill a gap as modelled.
detail: A lesson review asked that the app support each step of the procedure in independent practice, with each step appearing with a task that demonstrates it was done (`othello-course-renderer-draft/repo/docs/rules/pedagogy-and-lesson-structure.md`, lines 141-143). The course renderer adopted this as a rule: independent practice still walks the procedure, and each step gets a task proving the child did it, ending in a gap fill as modelled (lines 137-139). It is followed by convention, carried by the frame node's modelled, shared and independent row states (lines 148-149).
against: The same rules have step-by-step guidance fade across a unit: "Guide commentary before each part of a text, sentence starters and step-by-step guidance all fade." (`othello-course-renderer-draft/repo/docs/rules/pedagogy-and-lesson-structure.md`, lines 190-192). That rule is not yet applied, since only one lesson of the unit is authored (lines 207-208).

evidence.quote: **Rule.** Independent practice still walks the procedure. Each step gets a task proving the child did it: click the thing you are looking for, click the first line of the paragraph to reread, tap the evidence, then a gap fill as modelled.
The app still needs to support students to do each of these steps. **Have each step appear with a task that demonstrates they have done the step.**
Followed by convention; the `frame` node carries the modelled → shared → independent row state that makes this possible.
Guide commentary before each part of a text, sentence starters and step-by-step guidance all fade.
Only one lesson of the unit is authored, so nothing fades yet and no mechanism exists.
